text:
maya: seeing a big 5xx spike from model-serving pods in eu-west-1 after the autoscale event. Most errors are downstream egress failures to our artifact store and telemetry endpoints. any quick ideas? :panic:
raj: how widespread? just one AZ or cluster-wide?
sam: I caught a couple of kube-proxy logs showing RSTs when pods try to reach s3-redwood-internal (via privatelink). Could be endpoint health fallback to NAT.
maya: looks across two AZs. endpoint status shows "available" but traffic to the endpoint ENIs looks intermittent.
ops-bot: privatelink/endpoint/ep-01a2b3c health_check_changed -> UNHEALTHY at 2045678950 (from AWS)
raj: can you paste `ip route` from a node and `dig` results for the privatelink DNS name?
maya: sure, node1 output:
```
$ ip route show
10.0.0.0/16 via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0 proto static
169.254.0.0/16 dev lo scope link
0.0.0.0/0 via 10.0.0.254 dev eth0
```
`dig s3-redwood-internal.eu-west-1.private` returns the interface endpoint IPs (10.3.45.12, 10.3.45.13)

sam: ok. can you run `curl -v --resolve s3-redwood-internal.eu-west-1.private:443:10.3.45.12 https://s3-redwood-internal...` from the pod namespace? I want to see TLS & conn reset behavior.
maya: ran it, here's the tail:
```
* Connected to 10.3.45.12 (10.3.45.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
* Received HTTP/1.1 503
* Connection reset by peer
``` 
toni: 503 + immediate reset smells like conntrack on NAT instance hitting max entries and killing established mappings when fallback toggles. If privatelink health fluctuates, traffic might be flapping between ENI and NAT path causing conntrack collisions.
ryan: also check SGs on endpoint ENIs — I saw one of the ENIs had a stale egress rule blocking ephemeral ranges (32768-61000) after the last security cleanup.
raj: can you show `sudo nft list conntrack` or `conntrack -L | wc -l` on the NAT nodes?
sam: NAT instance shows 1.2M conntrack entries, max set to 1.5M but we saw a lot of TIME_WAIT churn. Also `/proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max` is default-ish. I recommend increasing nf_conntrack_max and short-term expanding ephemeral port range on NAT instances.
maya: also discovered route table for the worker subnets had two routes for 0.0.0.0/0: one to NAT GW via local RT and a higher priority route via TGW that was injecting a blackhole path for interface endpoint IPs. The route propagation from TGW was winning and packets to endpoint ENI were getting hairpinned back to TGW -> NAT -> outside, then returning via ELB which broke conntracking.
toni: ugh, TGW route propagation bias is a classic. We should restrict TGW propagation for these subnets or add an explicit route to the interface endpoint prefix to point to local ENIs (or use route priority/propagation filters).
ryan: quick patch: disabled TGW propagation for worker subnet RT → confirmed the route table now has explicit local route to the ENI CIDR. Also added an explicit /32 to the endpoint ENI IPs in the RT pointing to local ENI.
maya: updated SG on ENIs to allow ephemeral range egress (32768-61000) to pods' subnets and allowed established connections. Also bumped `nf_conntrack_max` to 3M and set `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established` to 86400 on NATs.
ops-bot: deploy/route-change approved and ran by ryan at 2045679020
sam: after changes, curl to endpoint returns 200 and model-serving error rate back down to baseline.
maya: verified across AZs, telemetry and s3 ops recovered. thanks all :thumbsup:
raj: follow-up action items: 1) add route propagation filters on TGW for privatelink CIDRs, 2) document SG checklist for endpoint ENIs, 3) tune conntrack on NAT autoscale launch configs, 4) add HealthCheck alert flapping threshold to avoid instant fallback.
toni: i'll open the infra-ops ticket with the checklist and assign to ryan + sam.
ryan: noted, will do the automation for conntrack tuning in ASG userdata.
maya: closing thread, will monitor for 24h and reopen if anything pops up :eyes:
ops-bot: incident resolved - privatelink egress flapping mitigated at 2045679115
